title: Representative phonogram transcript review samples
purpose: Calibrate narration conventions before reviewing the complete curriculum.

samples.ttsText: A. /ă/ as in apple. /ā/ as in apron. /ah/ as in father.
reviewQuestions: Should the single-letter symbol be spoken as the letter name before its sounds?
Are all three sound notations and examples instructionally accurate?
Should pauses separate each sound/example pair?

samples.ttsText: T H. Two letters. /th/ as in thin. /th/ as in this.
reviewQuestions: How should the voiced and unvoiced th sounds be distinguished in notation?
Is saying each letter name and then the two examples clear at the target pace?
Should a pause occur between the two sound/example pairs?

samples.ttsText: O O. Two letters. /oo/ as in moon. /oo/ as in book.
reviewQuestions: Should the two oo sounds use distinct phonetic notation?
Are moon and book the right contrastive examples for review?
Is the pause between the two examples long enough for repetition?

cuePhrases.useRestriction: used at the end of a word

samples.ttsText: E W. Two letters. /oo/ as in grew. /yoo/ as in new. Used at the end of a word.
reviewQuestions: Are /oo/ and /yoo/ clearly differentiated in the recorded wording?
Should the end-of-word restriction follow the examples or precede them?
Does the restriction need a longer pause for emphasis?

samples.ttsText: O U G H. Four letters. /ō/ as in though. /oo/ as in through. /ŭf/ as in rough. /ŏf/ as in cough. /aw/ as in thought. /ow/ as in bough.
reviewQuestions: Are all six sound notations and examples accurate and intelligible?
Should this long multi-sound record use a pause after every example?
Is the final bough example clear enough to distinguish /ow/?
